I will keep this year simple and steady. I farm in Quzhou County, so I will stay with the crop pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That fits our local weather, our soils, and the way I already know how to work. At my age, I do not want to spread myself across many crops that need more sorting, more marketing, and more delicate management. Wheat gives me grain and cash, and maize after wheat lets me use the land for the full year. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want stable emergence and better yield, but I will not push inputs too hard. I will fertilize at a medium level, irrigate wheat more because spring moisture is often not enough, and irrigate maize fewer times unless rain is poor. I will do ordinary pest control, not too many sprays, and I will use rotary tillage because it is what I can manage and what works reliably for me. My goal is not the highest possible yield; my goal is a crop I can finish well, with costs I can still carry and risks I understand.
